title_en: Yierku Company v. Wuxi City Administration for Industry and Commerce — dispute over administrative penalty for industry and commerce
ruling_gist_en: Detention, seizure, and administrative penalty are separate specific administrative acts. Where the administrative organ has informed the counterparty of the right to apply for administrative reconsideration, the right to institute administrative proceedings, and the time limit for instituting proceedings, and the counterparty fails to exercise the right to apply for reconsideration or institute proceedings within the statutory time limit regarding the detention or seizure, but later challenges the legality of the detention or seizure in an administrative lawsuit seeking revocation of the administrative penalty decision, the people's court shall, in accordance with the counterparty's claims, only review the legality of the administrative penalty act.
keywords_en: Administrative Law; Administrative Penalty; First Instance; Basic People's Court; Beijing; Jiangsu Province; Legal Person; State Organ; Product Quality Law; Legality Review of Detention and Seizure Acts; Supervisory Authority of Administrative Organs for Industry and Commerce over Commodity Quality in Circulation; Determination of Non-compliance of Product Labels with Regulations; Dismissal of Claims; Imported Styrene-Butadiene Rubber; Lack of Chinese Language and Safe Use Period on Product Labels; Industry and Commerce Inspection, Detention, and Seizure; Administrative Litigation
full_text_en:
Yierku Co., Ltd. v. Wuxi Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce — Administrative Penalty Case

Ruling Summary

Detention, sealing, and administrative penalties are separate and independent administrative acts. Where an administrative authority has informed the administrative counterparty of the right to apply for administrative reconsideration, the right to file a lawsuit, and the applicable time limit for filing a lawsuit, and the administrative counterparty fails to exercise the right to apply for reconsideration or to file a lawsuit within the statutory time limit regarding the detention or sealing, but later, in an administrative lawsuit seeking revocation of the administrative penalty decision, alleges that the detention or sealing was unlawful, the People's Court shall, in accordance with the administrative counterparty's claims, review only the legality of the administrative penalty.

Pursuant to the Product Quality Law and the *Provisions on the Functions, Internal Structure and Staffing of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce*, once a commodity enters the circulation sphere — regardless of whether it is stored in a warehouse, on a shelf, or at any other location — its quality is subject to supervision and administration by the administrative authorities for industry and commerce.

Where the outer packaging of an imported product with a limited period of use lacks Chinese-language labels, the foreign-language labels lack the safe use period or expiration date, and the production date is incomplete, such product does not comply with Article 27 of the Product Quality Law. If a seller sells such illegal products under serious circumstances, the seller shall, in accordance with Article 36 of the Product Quality Law, assume the liability for illegality provided for in Article 54 of the same Law.

Plaintiff: Beijing Yierku Science & Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Zengchan Road, Mentougou District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Wang Jianqiang, General Manager of the Company.

Defendant: Wuxi Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, Jiangsu Province, domiciled at: Jiankang Road, Wuxi.
Legal Representative: Sun Liancai, Director of the Bureau.

The Plaintiff, Beijing Yierku Science & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Yierku Company"), dissatisfied with the administrative penalty decision (Xi Gong Shang An [2003] No. 97) made by the Defendant, Wuxi Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as "Wuxi AIC"), filed a lawsuit with the Chong'an District People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province on June 3, 2004.

Plaintiff's Allegations: A batch of styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR) imported by the Plaintiff from Russia had been confirmed by the national commodity inspection authority as having passed quality inspection. This batch of SBR was stored in the warehouse of Wuxi Storage & Transportation Co., Ltd., Railway Transportation Branch (hereinafter referred to as "Wuxi Storage & Transportation Company") and had not been sold. The Defendant, on the grounds that the product labeling did not meet the requirements, detained and sealed this batch of SBR, and failed to notify the Plaintiff in a timely manner after the detention. On December 29, 2003, the Defendant issued the Penalty Decision (Xi Gong Shang An [2003] No. 97) imposing an administrative fine of RMB 119,000 on the Plaintiff. Article 26 of the *Provisions on Product Labeling and Marking* clearly states: "These Provisions shall be interpreted by the State Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision." This means that matters concerning product labeling and marking fall under the purview of the State Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision, not within the responsibilities of administrative authorities for industry and commerce. Furthermore, administrative authorities for industry and commerce may only supervise and inspect commodities that have entered the circulation sphere. The Plaintiff's SBR was stored in a warehouse and had not entered the circulation sphere; therefore, it was not within the Defendant's enforcement target. The Defendant abused its power, acted ultra vires, illegally detained and sealed the Plaintiff's property, illegally penalized the Plaintiff, and infringed upon the Plaintiff's lawful rights and interests. The Plaintiff requests the revocation of the administrative penalty decision (Xi Gong Shang An [2003] No. 97) made by the Defendant.

The Plaintiff submitted the following evidence:
1. Points 1, 4, and 5 of the *Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China* issued by the State Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision, to prove that matters concerning product labeling and marking are subject to supervision and inspection by the State Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision.
2. *Regulations on the Procedures for Formulating Rules* (promulgated by State Council Order No. 322 on November 16, 2001), to prove that the formulation of administrative rules reflects the unification of the administrative authority's functions and responsibilities; the power to interpret administrative rules belongs to the rule-making authority; if other State authorities consider that administrative rules conflict with laws or administrative regulations, they may submit written review proposals to the State Council, and the legal affairs agency of the State Council shall study and handle them.
3. Article 10 of the *Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China*, to prove that the Defendant's failure to promptly notify Yierku Company after detaining the goods was an illegal act.

Defendant's Defense: The SBR was a commodity imported by the Plaintiff for sale and falls within the scope of regulation under the *Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China* (hereinafter referred to as the "Product Quality Law"). This batch of SBR was a product with a limited period of use, and its product labeling did not comply with Article 27 of the Product Quality Law. The Defendant penalized the Plaintiff's illegal act in accordance with the Product Quality Law, based on clear facts, reliable evidence, correct application of laws and regulations, and compliance with statutory procedures. While imposing the administrative penalty for the illegal act, the Defendant safeguarded the Plaintiff's lawful rights and interests to the greatest extent possible, with the proper purpose of law enforcement. The administrative penalty decision made by the Defendant in accordance with the law does not involve abuse of power or ultra vires administration, and the Court should uphold it.

The Defendant submitted the following evidence:
1. Penalty decision, reconsideration decision, case investigation termination report, penalty decision approval form, case filing approval form, and source of leads record, to prove the legality of the law enforcement procedures;
2. On-site inspection record, to prove the model, quantity, and labeling status of the SBR stored by Yierku Company in the warehouse of Wuxi Storage & Transportation Company;
3. Transcript of witness testimony (interview with Wang Jianqiang, legal representative of Yierku Company), to prove the source, model, price, quantity, and labeling status of Yierku Company's goods;
4. Investigation record of witness Jia Mingwen, to prove the labeling status of SBR already sold by Yierku Company;
5. Letter from Yierku Company to the Economic Supervision and Inspection Detachment of Wuxi AIC, to prove the model, quantity of the SBR in question and the domestic sales situation of Yierku Company;
6. Special VAT invoices, to prove Yierku Company's previous purchases of SBR;
7. Special VAT invoices (counterfoil copy) and Special VAT invoices (deduction copy), to prove dealings between Yierku Company and Shandong Qingzhou Hongxin Materials Co., Ltd. regarding SBR;
8. Photographs, to prove that the outer packaging of the SBR in question had no Chinese-language labels, and the Russian-language labels did not indicate a complete production date, nor a safe use period or expiration date;
9. Photographs, to prove that the outer packaging of similar products already sold by Yierku Company also lacked Chinese-language labels, and the Russian-language labels did not indicate a complete production date, nor a safe use period or expiration date;
10. Russian-language labels, translation, and Chinese-language labels, to prove that the Russian-language labels on the outer packaging bags of the SBR in question did not indicate a complete production date, nor a safe use period or expiration date; and that the Chinese-language labels Yierku Company intended to use also did not comply with the relevant national standards and industry standards;
11. National standard for SBR (SBR) 1500 and industry standard for SBR (SBR) 1712, to prove that the quality guarantee period for the SBR in question was 2 years from the production date;
12. Case review form, list of detained items, financial processing documents, hearing notice, hearing transcript, trial report, etc., to prove that the coercive measures and penalty measures taken by Wuxi AIC were procedurally lawful;
13. Article 27, Paragraph 1, Item (4); Article 54; Article 49; and Article 18, Paragraph 1, Item (4) of the Product Quality Law, to prove the basis for Wuxi AIC's administrative acts including detention and penalty.

The Court presided over the cross-examination. After cross-examination, the Plaintiff, Yierku Company, argued: Evidence 1 of the Defendant, Wuxi AIC, was self-made by Wuxi AIC and cannot be used to prove the legality of Wuxi AIC's acts; Evidence 2 cannot be corroborated by other evidence, and its latter part is unrelated to the Plaintiff; Wuxi AIC did not present this evidence when making the administrative penalty decision; the translation in Evidence 10 is correct, but the Chinese-language labels are unclear; the trial report in Evidence 12 did not clearly describe the outer packaging status of identical domestic products; Article 27 of the Product Quality Law in Evidence 13 governs producers and sellers, not products in storage, and cannot serve as the basis for Wuxi AIC's law enforcement. Apart from these points, the Plaintiff raised no objections to the other evidence submitted by Wuxi AIC. The Defendant, Wuxi AIC, raised no objections to the legal bases submitted by the Plaintiff, Yierku Company, but contended that these bases did not achieve the Plaintiff's intended purpose of proof.

After cross-examination and verification, the Chong'an District People's Court of Wuxi found the following facts:

In March 2003, the Plaintiff, Yierku Company, imported 247.68 tons of SBR from TITAN Group (Russia). It stored 246.33 tons of this SBR, valued at RMB 1,991,505.35, in the warehouse of Wuxi Storage & Transportation Company, preparing for sale. On April 21, while inspecting the warehouse of Wuxi Storage & Transportation Company, the Defendant, Wuxi AIC, discovered that the outer packaging of this batch of SBR lacked Chinese-language labels, and the Russian-language labels also lacked the production month and day, as well as the safe use period or expiration date. On the same day, Wuxi AIC issued a Notice of Assistance in Detaining Property (Xi Gong Shang Jing Xie Zi [2003] No. 1003) to Wuxi Storage & Transportation Company, detaining this batch of SBR. On July 31, Wuxi AIC issued a Notice of Adoption of Administrative Compulsory Measures (Xi Gong Shang Qiang Zi [2003] Jing No. 0702), and in accordance with Article 18, Paragraph 1, Item (4) and Paragraph 2 of the Product Quality Law, sealed the 246.33 tons of SBR (Russian origin, including 61.89 tons of SBR-1500 and 184.44 tons of SBR-1705) stored by Yierku Company in the warehouse of Wuxi Storage & Transportation Company, and informed Yierku Company of its right to apply for reconsideration and to file a lawsuit. On August 8, Wuxi AIC issued a Notice of Adoption of Compulsory Measures (Xi Gong Shang Qiang Zi [2003] Jing No. 0705), detaining RMB 200,000 in cash from Yierku Company, lifting the seal on the company's SBR, and simultaneously informing Yierku Company of its right to apply for reconsideration and to file a lawsuit. Yierku Company did not apply for reconsideration or file a lawsuit within the statutory time limit regarding any of the above compulsory measures taken by Wuxi AIC. On September 27, Wuxi AIC held a hearing to hear Yierku Company's statements and defenses. On December 29, Wuxi AIC issued Decision No. Xi Gong Shang An (2003) No. 97, imposing the following penalty on Yierku Company: 1. Order to make corrections; 2. Fine of RMB 119,000 to be turned over to the State treasury. Yierku Company, dissatisfied, applied for administrative reconsideration with the Jiangsu Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce. That authority issued a Reconsideration Decision (Su Gong Shang Fu Zi [2004] No. 4) on March 30, 2004, upholding the administrative penalty decision (Xi Gong Shang An [2003] No. 97) of Wuxi AIC.

The issues in dispute in this case are: (1) In reviewing the legality of an administrative penalty, may the court simultaneously review prior administrative compulsory measures such as detention and sealing? (2) Does the administrative authority for industry and commerce have the power to investigate and deal with SBR stored in a warehouse? (3) Is the specific administrative act under suit illegal?

The Chong'an District People's Court of Wuxi held:

The Defendant, Wuxi AIC, successively took coercive measures of detention and sealing and decided on an administrative penalty against the property of the Plaintiff, Yierku Company. Detention, sealing, and administrative penalties are separate and independent specific administrative acts that an administrative authority may implement. When Wuxi AIC took the coercive measures of detention and sealing, it informed Yierku Company of its rights to apply for reconsideration and to file a lawsuit, as well as the time limit for filing a lawsuit. Within the statutory time limit, Yierku Company did not exercise its right to apply for reconsideration or to file a lawsuit regarding the coercive measures of detention and sealing. In this case, although Yierku Company alleged that all three specific administrative acts were illegal, it only requested the revocation of the administrative penalty decision. In accordance with Yierku Company's claim, the subject of review in this case should be Wuxi AIC's administrative penalty act; whether the detention and sealing acts were illegal is not within the scope of review in this case and will not be examined.

Article 8 of the Product Quality Law provides: "The product quality supervision department under the State Council shall be in charge of the supervision of product quality nationwide. The relevant departments under the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision of product quality within the scope of their respective functions and duties. The product quality supervision departments under the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be in charge of the supervision of product quality within their respective administrative areas. The relevant departments under the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the supervision of product quality within the scope of their respective functions and duties." Article 1 of the *Provisions on the Functions, Internal Structure and Staffing of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce* (issued by the General Office of the State Council under Guo Ban Fa [2001] No. 57) provides: "The function of supervising and managing the quality of commodities in the circulation sphere, originally borne by the State Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision, is hereby transferred to the State Administration for Industry and Commerce." Accordingly, it should be held that supervising and managing the quality of commodities in the circulation sphere is a function of the administrative departments for industry and commerce. The SBR imported by the Plaintiff, Yierku Company, from TITAN Group (Russia) had, through transfer, entered the circulation sphere; although this batch of SBR was stored in the warehouse of Wuxi Storage & Transportation Company, it was not for Yierku Company's own use but for sale; it was only because it was discovered that it had not been sold. Wuxi AIC's supervision and management of the quality of SBR that had entered the circulation sphere was not ultra vires. Yierku Company's argument that Wuxi AIC acted ultra vires is not accepted.

Article 36 of the Product Quality Law provides: "The labeling of products sold by sellers shall comply with the provisions of Article 27 of this Law." Article 27, Paragraph 1, Item (4) provides: "For products with a limited period of use, the date of production and the safe use period or expiration date shall be clearly marked in a conspicuous position." Article 15 of the *Provisions on Product Labeling and Marking* promulgated by the State Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision also provides: "For products with a limited period of use, the date of production and the safe use period or expiration date shall be indicated. The method of expressing the date shall comply with the provisions of the national standards or shall be expressed in the form of 'year, month, day.' The date of production and the safe use period or expiration date shall be printed on the product or on the sales packaging of the product." SBR is a product with a limited period of use. According to national standards and industry norms, the quality guarantee period for this product is 2 years from the date of production. On the outer packaging of the SBR imported by the Plaintiff, Yierku Company, from Russia, there were no Chinese-language labels; the only Russian-language labels indicated the production date only as "2003," without specifying the month or day. During the process of being investigated by the Defendant, Wuxi AIC, Yierku Company submitted Chinese-language labels for the product, but the production date on these Chinese-language labels was still "2003," without a specific month or day. The labels on the outer packaging of Yierku Company's SBR products violated the provisions of the Product Quality Law. When Wuxi AIC investigated, it followed procedures including case filing, investigation, and hearing. Based on clear illegal facts and reliable evidence, it made the administrative penalty decision, penalizing Yierku Company's illegal act. Wuxi AIC's administrative penalty act complied with the *Administrative Penalty Law* and the *Provisional Regulations on Procedures for Administrative Penalty by Authorities for Industry and Commerce*, and the procedures were lawful. Yierku Company was a seller of SBR. In making the penalty decision against Yierku Company, Wuxi AIC did not apply Article 36 of the Product Quality Law but directly invoked Article 27, which governs producers, to impose the penalty. Although the application of legal provisions was incomplete, this defect does not affect the legality of the administrative penalty act against Yierku Company.

In summary, the Chong'an District People's Court of Wuxi, in accordance with Article 54, Item (1) of the *Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, on August 25, 2004, rendered the following judgment:

Sustain the penalty decision (Xi Gong Shang An [2003] No. 97) made by the Defendant, Wuxi Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, on December 29, 2003.

Yierku Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, arguing: (1) The goods imported by the Appellant from Russia were still stored in a warehouse and had not entered the sales sphere; therefore, they should be governed by the *Law of the People's Republic of China on Import and Export Commodity Inspection*, and the administrative authority for industry and commerce had no power to inspect them. (2) Article 54 of the Product Quality Law provides that where product labels do not comply with Article 27, Item (4), a fine may only be imposed if the circumstances are "serious." The Appellee imposed a fine on the Appellant without factual basis for "serious circumstances." The Appellee's administrative penalty was based on unclear facts and erroneous application of law, and the first-instance judgment upholding it was erroneous. The Appellant requests the revocation of the first-instance judgment and the revocation of the Appellee's administrative penalty decision.

Wuxi AIC responded: The SBR imported from Russia was intended for sale and belonged to commodities that had entered the circulation sphere; the administrative authority for industry and commerce has statutory enforcement powers. The Appellant dealt in a large quantity of SBR, and it was verified that the labels on the SBR it sold in Shandong were also illegal. The Appellee's finding that the Appellant's illegal act had "serious circumstances" was based on facts. The first-instance judgment was based on clear facts and correct application of law and should be affirmed.

After review, the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found by the first-instance court. Additionally, based on the evidence cross-examined at the first instance, the court further found: The entity that applied to import SBR from TITAN Group (Russia) and was responsible for receiving the goods after importation was Manzhouli Yierku Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. After importing the SBR in question, Manzhouli Yierku Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. resold it to the Appellant, Yierku Company. Yierku Company is not a production enterprise; its main business scope is the sale of steel and chemical products. In May 2003, Yierku Company sold SBR products that lacked Chinese-language labels, whose Russian-language labels lacked the safe use period or expiration date, and whose production date was incomplete, to Shandong Qingzhou Hongxin Materials Co., Ltd.

The Wuxi Intermediate People's Court held:

After being imported from TITAN Group (Russia), the SBR in question had already undergone one transfer and entered the circulation sphere. As a non-production enterprise engaged in the sales of steel and chemical products, the Appellant, Yierku Company, was neither the producer nor the user of the SBR in question. Yierku Company purchased the SBR in question not for its own use but for sale; it was only because the goods were discovered in the warehouse that they were not sold. The facts of this case clearly reflect that the SBR in question had left the production sphere but had not yet entered the consumption sphere. However, whether the SBR in question was stored in a warehouse, on a shelf, or at any other location does not affect the fact that it had already entered the circulation sphere. Therefore, the first-instance finding that the SBR in question had entered the circulation sphere was not erroneous. The Appellee, Wuxi AIC, supervised and managed the quality of SBR that had entered the circulation sphere, which was an exercise of its statutory duties under the Product Quality Law, and there was no ultra vires act. Yierku Company's argument, based on the fact that the SBR in question was stored in a warehouse and had not yet been sold, that the matter should be governed by the *Law of the People's Republic of China on Import and Export Commodity Inspection* and that the authority for industry and commerce had no power to investigate, is not supported and is not accepted.

Article 54 of the Product Quality Law provides: “Where the product identification fails to comply with the provisions of Article 27 of this Law, a corrective order shall be issued; where the identification of packaged products fails to comply with the provisions of subparagraphs (4) and (5) of Article 27 of this Law and the circumstances are serious, an order shall be issued to stop production and sale, and a fine of not more than 30% of the value of the products illegally produced or sold shall be imposed; where there is illegal income, such income shall be confiscated.” The appellant Yierku Company distributed more than 240 tons of styrene-butadiene rubber valued at over RMB 1.9 million, involving a large distribution amount and quantity. It failed to affix proper identification on the outer packaging of the products as required by the Product Quality Law, and had already distributed part of this improperly identified styrene-butadiene rubber to Shandong. The appellee, Wuxi Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, accordingly determined that the illegal act of Yierku Company involved “serious circumstances,” which has a factual basis. Based on the illegal facts of Yierku Company, after going through procedures such as case filing, investigation, notification, and hearing, the Wuxi Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce imposed a fine of 6% of the value of the batch of products on the company, which complies with legal provisions. Yierku Company’s argument that there is no factual basis for “serious circumstances” and that the administrative penalty decision of the Wuxi Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce was erroneous is also not sustainable.

In summary, none of the grounds of appeal raised by the appellant Yierku Company are sustainable, and the appeal requests are not supported. The facts found by the judgment of first instance are basically clear, the application of law is correct, and the procedures are lawful, and the judgment should be affirmed. Accordingly, the Wuxi Intermediate People’s Court, in accordance with Article 61, paragraph (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China, rendered judgment on November 19, 2004:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.
